THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA
ORAL JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the judgment and award dated 02.01.2017 passed in M.V.C.No.162/2015 by the Prl. Senior Civil Judge, A.C.J.M and MACT, Puttur ('the Tribunal' for short).
2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.
3. Undisputedly there was an accident on 02.06.2014 at about 6.55 p.m. at Kudrabettu, Balthila village on Mangalore - Puttur road, while the petitioner as pillion rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 19/EJ-2760 (offending vehicle) moving towards Puttur NC: 2024:KHC:32282 side,
motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-19/Q-1639 came from opposite direction, hit the motor cycle of the petitioner.

entities.text: Prl. Senior Civil Judge, A.C.J.M and MACT, Puttur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Due to which, the petitioner has sustained injuries.

After taking treatment at A.J.
Hospital, Mangalore, under hospitalization for 87 days, the petitioner has approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-.
Claim was opposed by the insurance company.
The Tribunal after taking the evidence and hearing both the parties allowed the claim petition granting compensation of Rs.9,35,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum.
The insurance company has satisfied the said award.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement, the petitioner is before this Court on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri Vishwanatha Poojary K., learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.Mohankumar T., learned counsel for insurer of offending motor cycle.

2 NC: 2024:KHC:32282 5.
It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has suffered 8 fractures and dislocation, underwent six surgeries and spent huge money towards treatment.

Ex.P9 is the disability certificate, explains that the petitioner has suffered 10% upper limb disability and 90% lower limb disability, it goes to show that the petitioner has suffered more than 60% whole body disability, the Tribunal has assessed it only 33% which is on the lower side.
The Tribunal ignored the medical evidence and assessed the lesser whole body disability.
The nature of injuries certainly affecting in functioning of regular work as he was doing before the accident.

The petitioner was working as Site Supervisor in Devi Constructions and earning Rs.15,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has taken his income at Rs.7,000/-, compensation assessed towards loss of amenities and discomfort, loss of future income and loss of income during laid up is on lower side.

Per contra, learned counsel for the insurance company has contended that the accident involving two motor cycles, the Tribunal did not consider the contributory negligence on the part of the opposite vehicle.
The compensation awarded is proportionate to the nature of injuries, the petitioner has not suffered more than the disability as assessed by the Tribunal.
The person who issued the disability certificate is not the competent doctor and is only a forensic doctor.

By considering all these aspects and entirety of the case, the Tribunal has assessed just compensation and it is not a case for enhancement and has supported the impugned judgment.
7.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both parties and perused the records.
8. Ex.P3 is the wound certificate and Ex.P9 is the disability certificate issued by CW.1-Dr.Jayaprakash and CW.2-Dr.Ullas Shetty, who are the Forensic NC: 2024:KHC:32282 doctors.

As regarding nature of injuries, the medical evidence goes to show that the petitioner has suffered fracture of shafts of 2nd, 3rd and 4th metatarsal bones with crush injury of right foot,
fracture of lower end of right femur and comminuted fracture of upper end (neck) of right femur,
fracture of head of 5th metacarpal bone, fracture of proximal phalanx, fracture of middle phalanx,
fracture of distal phalanx and fracture of right hip.

Though CWs.1 and 2 are not the treated doctors, the nature of injuries goes to point out certain aspect of disability that being sustained by the petitioner who is aged 28 years as on the date of accident.
The nature of treatment and the surgeries clearly point out that the petitioner has suffered disability.

Even 10% of upper limb disability and 90% lower limb disability is taken into consideration, there NC: 2024:KHC:32282 is no evidence on record to show that what is the status of the petitioner as on the date of assessment.
The photographs shows in the disability certificate that the petitioner is bedridden but it is not so.
Considering all these aspects, the Tribunal has rightly assessed 33% whole body disability and it is just and proper.

3 10.

The petitioner claims that he was working as Manager/Site Supervisor in Devi Constructions and earning salary of Rs.15,000/- per month and even the owner of the said constructions was also examined as PW.2.
Ex.P10 is the salary certificate, which do not point out what are the projects that have been undertaken and in what manner he was working is not explained.
There is no Provident Fund details nor Profession Tax being deducted from the salary of the petitioner.
Hence, Ex.P10 cannot be relied as a guiding document to assess the income of the petitioner.
11. Accident is of the year 2014.
Even in the said period, a person with no proof of income will earn not NC: 2024:KHC:32282 less than Rs.8,500/- per month.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is taken as Rs.8,500/- per month instead of Rs.7,000/-.

The Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,00,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.1,70,000/- towards medical expenses, Rs.20,000/-
towards conveyance and Rs.50,000/- towards future medical expenses.
It is proper and retained as it is.

If the monthly income of the petitioner is taken at Rs.8,500/- for 9 months, the Tribunal has awarded lesser compensation at Rs.63,000/- towards loss of income during laid up and it has to be compensated with Rs.76,500/- (Rs.8,500/- x 9 months).
12. The petitioner has suffered multiple fractures.
The loss of amenities and discomfort assessed at Rs.30,000/- by the Tribunal is on lower side and same has to be taken at Rs.1,00,000/-.

The petitioner was under hospitalization for 87 days and therefore towards attendant charges, he is entitled to Rs.25,000/- instead of Rs.20,000/- assessed by the NC: 2024:KHC:32282 Tribunal and towards food and nourishment expenses for 3 months it comes to Rs.20,000/- instead of Rs.10,000/- assessed by the Tribunal.

13. As regarding loss of future income is concerned, the Tribunal has taken the income at Rs.7,000/-
per month and assessed the compensation at Rs.4,72,000/-.
The petitioner was aged 28 years as on the date of accident, applicable multiplier is '17', whole body disability is 33% and future prospects at 40% is to be added.
Then loss of future income comes to Rs.8,500/-+3,400(40%)=11,900/-x 12 x 17 x 33% =8,01,108/-.
There are no evidence to award compensation under the different heads.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled to total compensation of Rs.13,62,608/- as against Rs.9,35,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal, thereby enhancement of Rs.4,27,608/-, it is the just compensation which the petitioner is entitled in the facts and circumstances of the case.
